I think many of you heard about Eugene Podkletnov a Russian engineer who in 1990s found a way to negate gravity with EM propulsion. His way off achieving that reminds me of I.Filimonenko other Russian scientists that claims he invented it back in 1950s. #ufotwitter

More information about Eugene Podkletnov

In the 1990's, Dr. Podkletnov focused on researching an effect described as "gravity shielding" over a rotating YBCO superconductors, featured in the 1996 Wired Magazine article, "Breaking The Law Of Gravity". In the early 2000's, he collaborated with Dr. Giovanni Modanese on an Impulse Generator that utilized a Marx-generator discharge onto a superconducting emitter to generate a beam of gravitational force.  In 2020, he described a third experiment ion-impregnated gold foil on a rotating disk to generate gravity shielding without YBCO superconductors.

Five years ago, while testing a superconducting ceramic disc by rotating it above powerful electromagnets, Podkletnov noticed something extremely strange. Small objects above the disc seemed to lose weight, as if they were being shielded from the pull of Planet Earth. The weight reduction was small - around 2 percent - but nothing like this had ever been observed before. If the shielding effect could be refined and intensified, the implications would be immense. In fact, practical, affordable gravity nullification could change our lives more radically than the invention of the internal combustion engine.

In July 2002, an article by Nick Cook in Jane's Defence Weekly reported about Boeing's internal project GRASP — Gravity Research for Advanced Space Propulsion to evaluate the validity of Podkletnov's claims. The briefing obtained by Jane's says "If gravity modification is real, it will alter the entire aerospace business." The briefing allegedly says that Boeing, as well as BAE Systems and Lockheed Martin tried to approach Podkletnov directly and that "Podkletnov is strongly anti-military and will only provide assistance if the research is carried out in the 'white world' of open development."
